THEY TOOK THE “POWER UNITS” FROM HER LEG—AND INJECTED THEM INTO HER BLIND EYES.

What happened next has opened a completely new door in medicine.

A 26-year-old woman had suffered a devastating brain hemorrhage. The damage reached her optic nerves and retina, leaving her almost completely blind.

For 71 days before the procedure, doctors performed 45 automated tests.

Not one showed a normal pupil response to light.

Then the medical team tried something never previously reported in a human eye.

They removed a small piece of muscle from her leg.

From that tissue, they isolated fresh mitochondria—the microscopic structures that produce energy inside our cells.

The mitochondria were then injected directly into both eyes, 24 hours apart.

Within days, her pupils began responding to light again.

After treatment, 13 of 52 measurements reached the normal-response threshold. She was also reported to perceive shapes and shadows through her left eye.

But here is the part that matters:

The effect faded after approximately four weeks, and the procedure did not restore measurable vision.

This was one patient. The report has not yet completed peer review. It is not proof of a cure.

Yet the experiment crossed a boundary that would have sounded impossible not long ago:

Instead of replacing an entire damaged cell, scientists attempted to rescue it by transferring new biological “power units” into the tissue.

The question is no longer whether living mitochondria can be placed inside the human eye.

They already have been.

The real question is whether the effect can one day be made strong enough—and last long enough—to save vision.

Forward this to one person who needs to see where regenerative medicine is heading.

📌 NOSHAHR, Iran — President Masoud Pezeshkian inaugurates 158 projects of the Ministry of Roads and Urban Development in Mazandaran province worth about 23 trillion tomans, during an online ceremony marking Government Week.

​
According to Mohammad Shakibaei-Nasab, the managing director of the Ports and Maritime Organization, the projects were designed to expand transportation infrastructure, improve public welfare, and strengthen Mazandaran’s economic capacity, while two domestically built multipurpose maritime search-and-rescue vessels were launched in the maritime sector at a cost of more than 4.3 trillion rials.
​
Shakibaei-Nasab said the vessels will strengthen maritime search-and-rescue capabilities and improve the safety of maritime operations.
​
Meanwhile, four advanced marine loading arms were inaugurated at Amirabad and Noshahr ports.
​
Shakibaei‑Nasab said the equipment was designed and manufactured for loading and unloading petroleum products, with more than 2.4 trillion rials spent on the project.
​
Separately, the approximately 3.5‑kilometer road connecting Kolahduz‑Kala to Kohneh‑Kala in the Amirabad Port area was opened at a cost of more than 2 trillion rials.
​
Shakibaei‑Nasab said the road will improve access to Amirabad Port and strengthen transportation infrastructure in the surrounding area.
​
In the housing sector, 4,810 residential units were also inaugurated, including 1,915 urban and 2,895 rural units, with an investment of about 18 trillion tomans. A total of 150 plots of land were also allocated to applicants under a government program supporting families and population growth.
​
Other projects included 11 kilometers of transportation routes, a 40‑kilometer drainage, surface‑water collection, and sewage network at Sari Airport, and a weather station and meteorological buoy at Noshahr Port. ​
Meanwhile, 146 projects to eliminate accident‑prone areas and improve roads across the province were completed with more than 1.68 trillion tomans in investment. Historic moment: Tether has undergone a real audit for the first time

Remember the crypto market’s biggest fear all these years? “What if USDT isn’t actually fully backed?” That question is now settled. 

KPMG, one of the Big Four auditors, issued an unqualified opinion on Tether’s 2025 financial statements. This is the company’s first full audit in its entire history. They didn’t just check a “snapshot at a specific date” — they reviewed everything: the balance sheet, revenue, cash flows, and counterparties. All the way down to physically counting every gold bar in the vaults. Bottom line: reserves exceed liabilities by $6.8 billion.

🔎 Why didn’t this happen earlier? There are 3 reasons:

• Major auditors stayed away from crypto for years. There were simply too many scams and too much reputational risk surrounding the sector. Tether itself acknowledged that the company had long been a toxic client for the Big Four: in 2021, it paid fines to U.S. regulators over misleading disclosures about its reserves.

• There were no established accounting standards for valuing such a mix of assets: crypto, Treasuries, gold, and tokenized liabilities.

• Instead of audits, Tether published attestations. And an attestation is like a photo of a wallet at a specific moment: it shows that the money is there right now, but it doesn’t answer where it came from or where it went. An audit examines the entire picture over the course of a year.

💡 Why does this matter?

USDT is the lifeblood of the crypto market: nearly $185 billion is in circulation. As long as its backing was confirmed only through attestations, “Tether risk” remained one of the industry’s biggest systemic fears. And for institutions and regulators — especially in the U.S. — a Big Four audit is an essential ticket into the regulated financial world: without one, serious institutional money simply doesn’t enter the instrument.

Does this mean the market is about to reverse? No: an audit doesn’t print liquidity or move the price. But it removes one of the last barriers between crypto and major institutional capital.
